title: FertiBAY - Fertility-Preserving Surgery in Patients with Early-Stage Endometrial, Cervical, and Ovarian Cancer, as well as Atypical Endometrial Hyperplasia and Ovarian Borderline Tumors
summary:
Some women develop cancer of the uterus, cervix, or ovaries at a young age. As many of these women may still wish to have children later in life, it is important to preserve the possibility of a future pregnancy. In selected cases and depending on the tumor stage, so-called fertility-sparing surgery can be performed. The aim of this approach is to preserve the uterus or ovaries as much as possible in order to maintain fertility. The aim of this study is to investigate:

whether the cancer recurs,
whether the desire to have children can be fulfilled,
whether complications during pregnancy and childbirth occur more frequently,
and how women experience their quality of life after fertility-sparing surgery.

For this purpose, we will analyze data from women who previously underwent fertility-sparing surgery. This includes the evaluation of disease courses, possible recurrences, pregnancies, and other medical data. In addition, we would like to directly contact the patients. Through telephone interviews and questionnaires, we aim to learn how the women are doing today, whether they have had children, and how they assess their current quality of life and life situation. The goal of this study is to improve counseling and medical care for future patients with a desire to have children.
conditions: Carcinoma in situ of other and unspecified genital organs

interventions.name: Retrospective study of overall and recurrence-free survival, pregnancy and birth rates, and neonatal outcomes in patients who underwent fertility-preserving surgery  for early-stage endometrial, cervical, and ovarian cancer, as well as for atypical endometrial hyperplasia and borderline ovarian tumo

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients who underwent fertility-sparing surgery for endometrial cancer (C54.-), cervical cancer (C53.-), and ovarian cancer (C56.-)
Patients with borderline ovarian tumors (C56.-)
Patients with atypical endometrial hyperplasia (D07.0; N85.0; N85.1; N85.9)
Exclusion criteria:
Patients younger than 18 years and patients in whom a primary fertility-sparing approach was not performed are excluded from the study cohort. As the questionnaires are administered in German, patients who are unable to read or complete them are also excluded.
